{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "High frequency of vital signs and AE assessments at every visit",
      "quote": "Vital Signs |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and adverse events are collected at every visit, including all 15 post-screening visits, which is burdensome for patients and sites, especially for a chronic disease study with frequent visits.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital signs and AE assessments to key visits (e.g., every other visit) or allow remote collection for some visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical exam and ECG only at sparse visits may miss safety signals",
      "quote": "Physical Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Physical exam and ECG are only performed at screening, week 16, and end of study, leaving long gaps (e.g., from week 16 to week 36) without these safety assessments, which may be insufficient for a biologic with potential cardiac or systemic effects.",
      "fix": "Add physical exam and ECG at intermediate visits (e.g., every 8 weeks) or at least at EOT and EOS."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmological exam only at screening and EOS may miss treatment-emergent eye toxicity",
      "quote": "Ophthalmological Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmological exam is only at screening and end of study, with no on-treatment assessments, which is inadequate to detect potential ocular adverse events from the investigational drug.",
      "fix": "Add ophthalmological exams at least at EOT and possibly at an interim timepoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "PK sampling at every visit after baseline is excessive and burdensome",
      "quote": "Serum REGN3500 Concentration (PK) |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "PK samples are collected at nearly every visit (15 post-baseline visits), which is excessive for a monoclonal antibody with a long half-life and adds significant patient burden and site workload.",
      "fix": "Reduce PK sampling to sparse visits (e.g., trough at selected visits) and consider population PK approach."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sampling only at baseline, EOT, and EOS may miss early immunogenicity",
      "quote": "Anti-REGN3500 Antibody (ADA) |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ADA is only measured at baseline, week 16, and end of study, which may miss early ADA development that could affect PK and safety; more frequent sampling is typical for biologics.",
      "fix": "Add ADA sampling at least at week 8 and week 24, or align with PK sampling."
    },
    {
      "title": "Total IL-33 sampling at every visit is redundant with PK and adds burden",
      "quote": "Total IL-33 |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Total IL-33 is collected at the same frequency as PK, which is excessive for a pharmacodynamic biomarker; this adds blood draws and cost without clear added value.",
      "fix": "Reduce IL-33 sampling to match other biomarkers (e.g., hs-CRP, TARC) or to key timepoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Screening window of 35 days is long and may lead to rescreening issues",
      "quote": "V1 - D-35 to D-1 (Day -35)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "A 35-day screening window is unusually long and may allow disease status to change, requiring rescreening or affecting baseline comparability.",
      "fix": "Shorten screening window to 28 days or add a re-evaluation of eligibility if screening exceeds 28 days."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs predose and 30 min postdose windows are tight for dosing visits",
      "quote": "Vital signs (sitting blood pressure, pulse, and respiration rate) should be taken predose and 30 minutes (±10 minutes) postdose",
      "page": 53,
      "section": "8.2.3.1 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 30-minute postdose vital sign window (±10 min) is tight and may be difficult to coordinate with dosing procedures, especially if there are delays.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the postdose window to ±15 minutes or allow flexibility for clinic flow."
    }
  ]
}
